name: δ-Cadinene

pubchem.title: delta-Cadinene
pubchem.description: (+)-delta-cadinene is a member of the cadinene family of sesquiterpenes in which the double bonds are located at the 4-4a and 7-8 positions, and in which the isopropyl group at position 1 is cis to the hydrogen at the adjacent bridgehead carbon (the 1S,8aR-enantiomer). It is a delta-cadinene and a cadinene. It is an enantiomer of a (-)-delta-cadinene.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: δ-Cadinene is a volatile sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule that helps give many plants and essential oils their distinctive woody and herbal scents. As a fundamental building block in plant chemistry, it is often encountered in the fragrant oils of trees, herbs, and citrus fruits that we smell and taste every day.
consumer_summary.found_in: You can find it in familiar botanicals like hops (Humulus lupulus), tea tree (Melaleuca alternifolia), bitter orange (Citrus aurantium), and juniper (Juniperus communis).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to δ-cadinene because of its central role in plant defense systems, particularly how it acts as a precursor to protective compounds in crops like cotton. In human health, scientists are exploring its potential as a natural antioxidant and antimicrobial agent. The strongest evidence for these effects currently comes from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b), which are mapping how essential oils rich in this molecule interact with our biology.

structure_function.statement: Early work points toward a potential role in supporting physical comfort and pain relief.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether δ-cadinene can disrupt the growth cycle of certain abnormal cells, such as ovarian cancer cells. If this bears out, it could offer a new natural template for targeted therapies.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human clinical trial administering a standardized δ-cadinene extract alongside standard care to measure tumor marker progression and cell cycle arrest over 12 months.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early reviews point toward the possibility that volatile oils containing δ-cadinene might influence mood and ease depressive symptoms through olfactory pathways.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind human trial exposing participants with mild depression to inhaled δ-cadinene versus a placebo scent, measuring changes in standardized depression rating scales over 8 weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating whether this molecule can effectively deter insects, which would provide a natural alternative to synthetic bug sprays.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind field trial in humans comparing a topical δ-cadinene lotion to DEET and a placebo, measuring the number of mosquito landings per hour over a 6-hour period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether δ-cadinene can protect neurons from stress and damage, potentially offering a way to support long-term cognitive health.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: An animal study using a rodent model of neurodegeneration, administering oral δ-cadinene for 12 weeks to measure cognitive performance in maze tests and neuronal survival in brain tissue.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b) looking at its antimicrobial and antioxidant properties; most of the rest is animal and lab research.
